The city of Sacramento is located in California.
The population of Sacramento was 524,943 as of 2020.
Sacramento is the capital city of the U.S. state of California.
Sacramento is also the seat of Sacramento County.
The confluence of the Sacramento and American Rivers is where Sacramento is situated.
The Sacramento Valley is part of Northern California.
The population of Sacramento makes it the fourth-most populous city in Northern California.
The population of Sacramento makes it the sixth-most populous city in the state of California.
The population of Sacramento makes it the ninth-most populous state capital in the United States.

Old Sacramento is part of the city's history.
Before Spanish arrival, the area was inhabited by Nisenan, Maidu, and other indigenous peoples.
Gabriel Moraga named the Río del Santísimo Sacramento (Sacramento River) in 1808 after the Blessed Sacrament.
Juan Bautista Alvarado granted John Augustus Sutter responsibility for colonizing the Sacramento Valley in 1839.
John Augustus Sutter established Sutter's Fort and the settlement at Rancho Nueva Helvetia in 1839.
Sutter's Fort was built on a Mexican land grant of 50,000 acres (20,000 ha) by John Sutter Sr. in 1839.
The American Conquest of California and the 1848 Treaty of Guadalupe-Hidalgo led to the development and incorporation of the waterfront developed by Sutter as the City of Sacramento in 1850.
In 1852, the city offered its county courthouse to the state of California to house the state legislature.
The city became the permanent state capital in 1854.
The construction of a new state capitol building was finished in 1874.
Sacramento is the fastest-growing major city in California.

Sacramento is home to California State University, Sacramento and UC Davis.
Sacramento is a major center for the California healthcare industry.

The city receives 15.3 million visitors per year according to the Sacramento Convention and Visitors Bureau in 2013.

Nisenan, Maidu, and other indigenous peoples lived in the area for perhaps thousands of years before Spanish arrival.
Gabriel Moraga named the Río del Santísimo Sacramento (Sacramento River) after the Blessed Sacrament in 1808.
John Augustus Sutter established Sutter's Fort and the settlement at Rancho Nueva Helvetia in 1839.
Sutter Sr. called his colony New Helvetia, a Swiss-inspired name.
The colony began to grow as more pioneers headed west.
Sutter Sr. received 2,000 fruit trees from which the agriculture industry in the Sacramento Valley started.
James Marshall discovered gold at Sutter's Mill in Coloma in 1848.
Numerous gold-seekers came to the area increasing the population.
John Sutter Jr. arrived in August 1848 to assist his father in reducing debt.
The Sutters struggled to contain thousands of new gold miners and prospectors.
Sutter's Fort, Mill, and the town of Sutterville eventually failed.
In 1850, Sacramento was incorporated as a city.
A flood devastated the city on January 10, 1850.
Hardin Bigelow, the first elected mayor, led efforts to build the city's first levee in early 1852.
The new levee broke during the first major storm of the season and the city flooded again.
A new levee was built for $50,000 but also broke.
Between October and December 1850, a cholera epidemic killed 1,000 residents including Mayor Bigelow and 17 physicians.
In November 2, 1852, the Great Conflagration burned more than 80 percent of the city's structures.
Within a month, 761 structures were rebuilt, many in brick.
The California State Legislature moved to Sacramento in 1854.
The capital under Spanish and Mexican rule was Monterey.
The first Constitutional Convention and state elections were held in Monterey.
San Jose was decided as the new state's capital.
From September 9, 1850 through 1851, the legislature met in San Jose.
It moved to Vallejo in 1852 and Benicia in 1853 before ending up in Sacramento in 1854.
During the 1850s, Sacramento was consolidated with the County of Sacramento.
The Sacramento Constitutional Convention of 1879 named Sacramento as the permanent state capital.
Sacramento covers an area of 100.1 square miles (259 km²).
81% of it is land and 2.19% is water.
The depth to groundwater is typically about 30 feet (9 m).
Much of the land west of the city in Yolo County is reserved for a vast flood control basin due to historical vulnerability to floods.
The city is at the confluence of the Sacramento River and the American River.
It has a deep-water port connected to San Francisco Bay through the Sacramento–San Joaquin River Delta.
Sacramento is known as the "City of Trees."
The term was first recorded in 1855.
The city has more trees per capita than any other city in the world.
Trees were initially scarce due to lack of trees, but cottonwood and eucalyptus varieties were later planted.
Later, locust, willow, elm, and palm trees were also planted.
It was the first US city to be designated a City of Trees by the Arbor Day Foundation in 1978.

Chinatown was on "I" Street from Second to Sixth Streets, called the China Slough.
It was considered a health hazard due to its location within a levee zone.
Throughout its history, there were fires, acts of discrimination, and prejudicial legislation such as the Chinese Exclusion Act.
The mysterious fires were thought to be set by those who resented the Chinese working class.
Ordinances on building material were set to try to get the Chinese to move out.
Newspapers wrote stories that portrayed the Chinese in an unfavorable light.

The oldest part of town besides Sutter's Fort is Old Sacramento.
It consists of cobbled streets and historic buildings from the 1850s and 1860s.
Buildings have been preserved, restored, or reconstructed.
The district is now a substantial tourist attraction with rides on steam-powered historic trains and horse-drawn carriages.

Sacramento has a hot-summer Mediterranean climate (Köppen Csa).
The normal annual mean temperature is 61.8°F (16.6°C).
Summer heat can be moderated by the "delta breeze" coming through the Sacramento–San Joaquin River Delta.
Foggiest months are December and January.
Tule fog can lower visibility to less than 100 feet.
Snowfall is rare, with only three significant snow accumulations since 1900.
